oil.when: 2011–2014 (MENU button and thumbwheel on the turn signal lever)
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Use the MENU button and the thumbwheel on the turn signal lever to scroll to REMAINING OIL LIFE.
Press SET/CLR to reset the oil life to 100%.
When it asks, roll the thumbwheel to YES and press SET/CLR to confirm.
oil.note: Checked in the 2011 and 2014 owner's manuals. Do not reset it at any other time, because the reading cannot be put back.

oil.when: 2016 redesigned Cruze (not the 2016 Cruze Limited, which carries the older car's controls)
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition on and bring REMAINING OIL LIFE up on the instrument display.
Base display: press and hold SET/CLR on the turn signal lever while oil life is showing. Larger display: press and hold the check-mark (select) button on the steering wheel instead.
If that does not work: with the ignition on and the engine off, press the accelerator pedal fully to the floor and release it three times within five seconds.
Start the car and check that the oil life reads 100% and the CHANGE ENGINE OIL SOON message is gone.
Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the Tire and Loading Information label on the driver's door pillar.
There is no reset button. The low tire pressure light stays on until the pressure is corrected, then goes off on its own after a short drive.
tpms.note: If the light comes on only on cold mornings and goes off as you drive, a tire is getting low: check and top up the pressures.
